newsitem.title: USA: Sears to pay $100 mln to settle US FTC charges.
newsitem.headline: Sears to pay $100 mln to settle US FTC charges.

text.p: Sears will make refunds of about $100 million to consumers who continued to make payments or face illegal collection efforts after their Sears account debts were discharged in bankruptcy proceedings, the Federal Trade Commission said Wednesday.
The FTC said Sears had induced customers who had filed for bankruptcy protection to reaffirm their debts to Sears in return for keeping their Sears credit cards or merchandise.

"Sears falsely represented that these reaffirmation agreements would be filed with the bankruptcy courts, as required by law, and that the consumers would be legally obligated to pay," the FTC said in a statement.
But the FTC said that in many cases, Sears never filed the agreements or bankruptcy courts did not give their approval, and therefore the agreements were not binding.

The FTC said more than 200,000 Sears customers may have been affected. The FTC action was coordinated with settlement of a class action lawsuit against Sears which will be submitted to the U.S. bankruptcy court in Boston on Thursday.
The FTC said this practice began in 1985.
